routes.label: Use distances on the number line

question: For \(x\) real, the inequality \(1\le\lvert x-2\rvert\le7\) is equivalent to:
solution:
The quantity \(\lvert x-2\rvert\) is the distance from \(x\) to \(2\) on the number line. That distance must be at least \(1\) and at most \(7\).

To the left of \(2\), the allowed points run from \(2-7=-5\) to \(2-1=1\). To the right, they run from \(2+1=3\) to \(2+7=9\). Every point in these intervals has an allowed distance, and every point outside them violates one of the bounds.

All four endpoints are included because both inequalities allow equality. Thus
\[
-5\le x\le1
\quad\text{or}\quad
3\le x\le9,
\]
which is choice D.
